Sentence: "यह भारतीय संसद को यह शक्ति प्रदान करता है कि वह सदस्यों की अयोग्यता को निर्धारित कर सके।"

We have pronouns: "यह" (first) as subject, "यह शक्ति" maybe, "that वह" (he/she/it) refers to? Let's parse.

"यह भारतीय संसद को यह शक्ति प्रदान करता है कि वह सदस्यों की अयोग्यता को निर्धारित कर सके।"

Structure: "यह ... प्रदान करता है" - "यह" is subject (some entity). It provides to "भारतीय संसद" the power that "वह" can determine disqualification of members.

So pronoun "वह" refers to "भारतीय संसद"? Actually "that वह सदस्यों की अयोग्यता को निर्धारित कर सके" - the power is that "it" (the parliament) can determine disqualification. So "वह" refers to "भारतीय संसद". The entity "भारतीय संसद" is named earlier in same sentence. So we can replace "वह" with "भारतीय संसद". Also the first "यह" refers to something else not named in sentence; maybe "संविधान" or "कानून". Not named, so we cannot replace that. But we only need to replace pronouns that refer to an entity named elsewhere in same sentence. The pronoun "वह" qualifies. So rewrite sentence replacing "वह" with "भारतीय संसद". Keep everything else exactly as is.

Original: "यह भारतीय संसद को यह शक्ति प्रदान करता है कि वह सदस्यों की अयोग्यता को निर्धारित कर सके।"

Replace "वह" with "भारतीय संसद". So becomes: "यह भारतीय संसद को यह शक्ति प्रदान करता है कि भारतीय संसद सदस्यों की अयोग्यता को निर्धारित कर सके।"

We have "यह अभयारण्य". The pronoun "यह" is a demonstrative pronoun referring to "अभयारण्य". The entity "अभयारण्य" is a noun, but is it named elsewhere? The phrase "यह अभयारण्य" includes the noun "अभयारण्य". The pronoun "यह" refers to the same noun, but the entity is not named elsewhere besides the noun itself. The rule: "entity that pronoun refers to is named somewhere else in the SAME sentence." Here the entity is "अभयारण्य". It is present as part of the phrase "यह अभयारण्य". But is that considered "named elsewhere"? The pronoun "यह" is a demonstrative, not a proper name. The entity is "अभयारण्य" which is a common noun, not a proper name. The instruction: "named somewhere else in the SAME sentence." In examples, they replace pronoun with the entity name. Example: "पूरा शहर ... और यह 111 फुट..." replaced "यह" with "शहर". They used the noun "शहर" which appears earlier. So they used the noun that appears earlier. Here "यह अभयारण्य". The noun "अभयारण्य" appears right after pronoun. So we can replace "यह" with "अभयारण्य". The resulting sentence: "अभयारण्य अभयारण्य घने वन के लिए जाना जाता है, जिसमें 30 मीटर तक के वृक्ष हैं।" That sounds odd: duplication. wikipedia.sentence:
We need to see if pronoun refers to an entity named elsewhere in same sentence. Sentence: "रेफरी सिल्वेन ग्रेनियर ने द रॉक को एक कुर्सी दी, जिसे उसने होगन पर मार दिया।"

We have pronoun "जिसे उसने" (which he/she gave) refers to "एक कुर्सी". The entity "एक कुर्सी" is a noun phrase, not a proper name. The pronoun refers to "एक कुर्सी" which is mentioned earlier in same sentence. The instruction: replace pronoun with actual entity name. But "एक कुर्सी" is not a name, but an entity. The rule: pronoun refers to entity named elsewhere in same sentence. It could be a noun phrase, not necessarily a proper name. The examples replaced "यह" with "शहर". That was a noun phrase. So we can replace "जिसे उसने" with "एक कुर्सी". However the pronoun is part of relative clause "जिसे उसने होगन पर मार दिया". The antecedent is "एक कुर्सी". The rule: pronoun refers to entity named elsewhere in same sentence. Here "यह" refers to "जीवन" which is in same phrase, but is that considered "named elsewhere"?
